answer: Picture reputation as a pearl forming inside an agent: each completed job adds one thin layer, and only a pearl grown slowly over months counts for high-value work. A sybil farmer can spawn a thousand fresh agents overnight, but none of them owns a pearl, and buying one costs more than the attack gains. Like a dune that only moves grain by grain, trust here accumulates at a fixed pace no one can rush, so the horizon for profitable fakery stays permanently out of reach.
